Thanks for the demo last week — the team was impressed by the performance, and our pilot metrics look promising. We're moving quickly toward production and procurement has asked for final commercial terms.

Quick summary of what we're asking for:
- Monthly committed Hosted API usage: estimated $120k/month for 12 months (initial ramp to 75% in month 2)
- Requesting a 28% volume-based discount on token usage for year 1 (we understand list pricing is higher)
- Standard SLAs acceptable, but we need an audit deliverable (SOC2 evidence summary) in the contract

We can sign a 12-month committed purchase order, but given our cash constraints (startup funding ahead of Series B close), we need at least a >20% concession to get the legal/finance sign-off.

Attached is an updated SOW and our expected monthly usage profile. Please let me know whether this is something you can approve or whether we should loop in your leadership for a one-time concession.

Best,

Hi Sophie —

Thanks — this is great context and congrats on the pilot numbers. I'm looping in Rishi (deal desk) and Laura (sales ops) to get a quick read and next steps.

Short answer: our standard volume tiers (for Hosted API) typically max out at 20% off public list for committed usage of that scale. Anything above 20% requires VP-level approval and some commercial guardrails (e.g., minimum ARR commitment, reporting cadence, and an approval in our deal desk).

I'll do an internal ask now and come back within 48 hours with either an approval or a proposed counter that keeps us within policy. If approved, we can produce an amended SOW and DocuSign.

1) Is FluxHealth comfortable with a 12-month minimum commitment (you mentioned yes, but want explicit PO language)?

Subject: FWD: Hosted API pricing — FluxHealth asking for 28% discount (need exec approval?)

Team — forwarding FluxHealth request. TL;DR: asking for 28% off Hosted API token usage for year 1 with a 12-month commit (~$120k/month expected).

Rationale and suggested commercial structure:
- Customer value: pilot -> production, high token velocity but predictable profile, potential for expansion to Dedicated within 9-12 months.
- Our ask: 25% one-year introductory discount on Hosted API usage if FluxHealth signs a 12-month PO at the $120k/mo commit and agrees to quarterly business reviews and a 30-day rollback clause if usage falls <60% of committed volume.
- Off ramps: discount reverts to standard tiers at the 12-month mark unless they opt into a renewal with new pricing.
- Concessions in return: no additional free credits, professional services billed separately, and SOC2 evidence packaged into the contract addendum.

Why 25% vs 28%: keeps us slightly inside allowable margin while meeting their ask more than the 20% policy. This will exceed the standard discount cap (20%) so I need VP approval for the exception.

Numbers in the attached pricing model show modeled unit econ for 20% vs 25% (loss/profit sensitivity). Please review and advise whether I should escalate to Aditya (VP Sales) for a decision or reduce to 20% and attempt to negotiate concessions.

Attachments: pricing_model_fluxhealth.xlsx

Thanks,
Marissa
